“I remember returning a library book that was years late. I was at the library, and the librarian unfolded my old checkout slip. That little bit of paper made me feel more embarrassed than handing over the book had. Then there was the due date stamped inside the cover—it’s one thing to know you’re late, and another to see the actual date sitting there.

“I kept wondering what the librarian thought of me. I can’t say what they actually thought, but I felt very conspicuous. I wanted to explain, except I didn’t have an explanation that would make it less late. Dates are funny—I enjoy looking up at stars and thinking about enormous stretches of time, but that small stamped date was quite enough time for me to think about just then.”
